title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 1 of a 'Rétrospection sur les cartes (finies)', a summary preceded by the table of contents on page 50. It recapitulates Grothendieck's combinatorial description of maps (dessins).

(1) Definition. A topological cellular map is a compact surface X, not necessarily orientable, with a closed subset K locally homeomorphic to a star (a topological 1-complex). Two 'cellular' hypotheses are imposed: (a) K has no connected component homeomorphic to S^1 and no isolated point; (b) the components of X−K are open discs. The marginal note seems to say that (b) forces K to be connected when X is, given that K is nonempty and not reduced to a point. This is the usual cellular-embedding condition.

Maps are taken up to isotopy, giving an 'isotopy category'. Using 'biarcs' (flags, i.e. triangles of the barycentric subdivision, also called 'repères') one gets an equivalence of categories: isotopy classes of finite maps ≃ finite 'special' Γ2-sets.

Here Γ2 = <τ0, τ1, τ2 | τ0² = τ1² = τ2² = (τ0τ2)² = 1> is the cartographic group, a Coxeter-type group isomorphic to (Z/2×Z/2) * Z/2. 'Special' means that τ0, τ1, τ2 and τ0τ2 act without fixed points; this excludes boundary and degenerate edges.

Notation notes. τ2 will be written τ∞, which suits the link with algebraic geometry (the points 0, 1, ∞ of P^1). The marginal note says the indexing σ_i or τ_2 is better suited to higher-dimensional and Coxeter generalisations. He also sets ρ1 = τ0τ∞.

(3) The oriented subgroup Γ2^0 is the kernel of the map Γ2 → Z/2 sending each τ_i to 1. (4) It has presentation <ρ0, ρ1, ρ∞ | ρ∞ρ1ρ0 = 1, ρ1² = 1>. The next page gives ρ∞ = τ1τ0, ρ1 = τ0τ∞, ρ0 = τ∞τ1, so Γ2^0 ≅ Z * Z/2. This is the oriented cartographic group whose finite quotient sets correspond to oriented maps, and which links maps to coverings of P^1 − {0, 1, ∞} branched with ramification index ≤ 2 over 1.

The purpose is to set up the later sections listed on the contents page: weighted triangular maps, Π_{0,3}, signature groups, and polygonal maps.
errors: No mathematical errors. Check: ρ∞ρ1ρ0 = τ1τ0·τ0τ∞·τ∞τ1 = 1, and ρ1² = (τ0τ2)² = 1, so the presentation (4) is consistent. Reidemeister–Schreier confirms that the index-2 kernel of (Z/2×Z/2)*Z/2 is Z*Z/2.
Minor gap: the equivalence (1) is stated without the connectedness conventions or the precise definition of morphisms in the isotopy category, but this is a retrospective summary.

ideas.what: Cartographic group Γ2 = <τ0, τ1, τ2 | τ_i² = (τ0τ2)² = 1> and the equivalence between finite maps (up to isotopy) and finite Γ2-sets with fixed-point-free conditions, via flags/biarcs

ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on 'cartes' and the cartographic group

deep.surprise_reason: This is a self-recap of the cartographic group and the oriented cartographic group, essentially as published in Esquisse d'un programme and contemporaneous work by Jones–Singerman. Nothing new beyond notational remarks.
transcription_corrections: 'de bicar[?]' should read 'de biarc' (the term is used on the next page).
Relation (4) reads 'ρ∞ρ1ρ0 = ρ1² = 1'; there is a crossed-out symbol before ρ1², not an ellipsis to be filled in.
In (2), τ2 is underlined with 'ou τ∞' written beneath it.
The top marginal note appears to say that b) implies K is connected if X is connected, provided K is nonempty and not reduced to a point (consistent with the added 'ni de point isolé').
